subject: fieldIndex: Threshold to differentiate only not health plants

messages.author: 840f9155920fe615
messages.subject: fieldIndex: Threshold to differentiate only not health plants
parts:
Is there some approach or some empirical threshold value for the image segmentation using red/green relation present in the SCI vegetation index (like for soil from the plants in fieldIndex)? My goal is to find only not healthy (yellowish, browning or not green) plants the image.
Thanks in advanced,
Alexandre

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: fieldIndex: Threshold to differentiate only not health plants
parts:
Hi Alexandre,

I don't know a specific index for differentiating browning plants from the soil. However, as a suggestion you can use a mask from when the plants were green to remove the soil. In other words, if you toke a picture before the disease causes changes on colors, you can make a mask and apply this mask on the mosaic with the disease. In this case geographic corrections (e.g. with GPC) are important to make the overlays of mosaics. Here is an example how to do it (EX3.RemSoil on "Removing soil"): https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P13 
 
Another suggestion is to make a mask using a thermal camera and apply this mask on the RGB mosaic. You can easily differentiate plants (healthy or not) from the soil.

Another possibility is to use the function fieldMask more than once. For example, you first remove the green plants. Then you can use the output "newMosaic" to find other index to differentiate the browning/yellowish plants from the soil. As a suggestion, to calculate area (fieldArea, fieldCount, or fieldObject) you can use "is.na(mask)<-1".

Let me know if this helps you or if you have more questions.
All the best,
Filipe
